title: State Mental Health Agency Expenditures and Funding Sources: FY'2001 to FY'2024 (NRI 2024-2025 State Profiles), Table 1: State Mental Health Agency Expenditures for Mental Health, FY 2024
table_footnote: FY 2024 Expenditures from SAMHSA URS Table 7a
highlights_text: Highlights based on 50 States, DC and Puerto Rico: FY 2024 data from the SAMHSA Uniform Reporting System, earlier data from NRI's SMHA Revenues and Expenditures Study. In state fiscal year 2024, the 50 states, District of Columbia and Puerto Rico spent $61.4 billion to provide mental health services to 8.1 million individuals. States averaged $179 per resident for mental health expenditures. ... SMHAs expended 73% of their funds ($45.0 billion) for community-based mental health services, and 24% ($14.8 billion) for care in state psychiatric hospitals, with central and regional SMHA offices accounting for the remaining 3% ($1.6 billion).
method: PDF fetched same-origin in the browser; text extracted in JS from the page-5 content streams (FlateDecode + ToUnicode CMaps), rows parsed by regex. Integrity checks done in JS: for all 52 rows per-capita = total / civilian population to the cent; the 52 totals sum to the printed Total ($61,398,388,761) and populations to 342,326,370.
notes: Ranks are out of 52 (50 states, DC, Puerto Rico). The 'Total' row ($179.36 per capita) includes Puerto Rico and is used for the US row. Alabama: $133.15 per capita, rank 30; 84.8% community, 14.2% state hospital (Table 2). Table 1's printed 'Average' ($188.30) and 'Median' ($159.51) rows were not used.
